dimensions.assessment: Affects millions of adults at higher risk for glaucoma, including those 40 or older of African, Hispanic/Latino, or Asian ancestry, individuals with specific clinical risk factors, adults 60 and older, and participants in various health programs.
dimensions.evidence: Approximately 4.22 million people in the United States were living with glaucoma in 2022

dimensions.assessment: Provides significant clinical benefits by establishing mandatory, zero-cost-sharing annual glaucoma screenings and expanded treatment grants, improving early detection for conditions that can cause blindness.
dimensions.evidence: Each contract under this chapter shall require the carrier to provide benefits for screening for glaucoma... without imposition of any cost sharing

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes $10,000,000 for CDC glaucoma detection and prevention programs and $10,000,000 for NIH research for fiscal years 2027 through 2028, alongside wider mandatory health coverage requirements.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $10,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2027 through 2028.

dimensions.assessment: Amends multiple major federal statutes including the Public Health Service Act, Social Security Act, and title 5 of the United States Code to mandate coverage across private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, and FEHB.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2713 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300gg-13) is amended... with respect to specified individuals... screening for glaucoma

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent statutory mandates on health insurance plans starting in January 2027, alongside temporary two-year appropriations for specific grant programs.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this subsection shall apply with respect to plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2027.

summary: The Glaucoma Vision Act of 2026 requires various public and private health insurance programs to cover annual glaucoma screenings for specified high-risk individuals without cost-sharing. It also establishes CDC grants for glaucoma detection and prevention programs, and NIH research grants for glaucoma and optic nerve damage.

affected_groups.effect: Gain guaranteed coverage for annual glaucoma screenings across private insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, and FEHB plans starting January 1, 2027, generally without cost-sharing.
affected_groups.group: Specified individuals aged 40 or older with certain ancestries or clinical risk factors, and individuals aged 60 or olde

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to receive free or low-cost glaucoma screenings and follow-up treatment through CDC-funded grant programs.
Required to update plans to provide zero-cost-sharing annual glaucoma screening coverage for qualifying populations beginning in 2027.
affected_groups.group: Health insurance providers (Private, Medicare, Medicaid, FEHB)

key_provisions: Requires private health insurance plans, Medicare, Medicaid, and Federal Employees Health Benefits plans to cover annual glaucoma screenings for specified individuals without cost-sharing starting January 1, 2027.
Defines specified individuals to include adults aged 40 or older with certain ancestral backgrounds or clinical risk factors, and all individuals aged 60 or older.

Directs the CDC Director, through the Vision Health Initiative, to expand detection and prevention activities by awarding competitive grants for free or low-cost screenings and treatment to uninsured and underinsured high-risk individuals.
Authorizes $10 million for fiscal years 2027 through 2028 for the CDC glaucoma detection and prevention program, prioritizing underserved populations and racial and ethnic minority communities.
Authorizes $10 million for fiscal years 2027 through 2028 for the NIH to award competitive research grants related to glaucoma and optic nerve damage, including gene and stem cell therapies.
missing_information: Exact total federal appropriations beyond the specific $10 million authorizations for CDC and NIH grants for fiscal years 2027 through 2028 are not detailed.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Glaucoma Vision Act of 2026 requires various public and private health insurance programs to cover annual glaucoma screenings for specified high-risk individuals without cost-sharing. It also establishes CDC grants for glaucoma detection and prevention programs, and NIH research grants for glaucoma and optic nerve damage.
summary_detail.significance: The bill expands preventative health access by mandating zero-cost-sharing glaucoma screenings across nearly all major U.S. health insurance sectors for targeted demographics, while allocating federal funding toward targeted detection programs and advanced medical research.

title: Glaucoma Vision Act of 2026
